overview: LiquidSense Dev's InvMove keeps the player moving while a screen is open by re-asserting the raw keyboard state into the movement keybinding pressed flags on every UpdateEvent. The handler excludes GuiChat and the pause menu outright, and the NoDetectable switch adds a second carve-out: when it is on, the current screen must not be a GuiContainer, so movement only survives on non-container screens. The AACAdditionPro switch is a display tag only and changes nothing in the handler, and the NoMoveClicks switch cancels every ClickWindowEvent while the player is moving so the forced walk cannot be paired with a GUI click. The wire fingerprint is the same as every inventory-move module: the C03 position stream keeps advancing while a server-side container is open.

sections.p: The module never touches packet code. onUpdate fires once per tick and, when the screen guard passes, writes GameSettings.isKeyDown(keyBindForward) into keyBindForward.pressed for forward, back, right, left, jump and sprint. The vanilla input classes read those flags (MovementInputFromOptions calls getIsKeyPressed), so the player entity keeps producing movement input while a chest, furnace or inventory screen has focus. Because the write happens on the pre update event, the forced state is in place before the tick's movement is computed, and the C03 variant that tick carries nonzero position deltas. The NoDetectable carve-out inverts the guard: with the switch on, the handler only runs when the current screen is not a GuiContainer, which excludes exactly the container screens the inventory-move checks watch.

NoMoveClicks is the anti-mistake companion: onClick cancels any ClickWindowEvent while MovementUtils.isMoving() reports forward or strafe input, so a player holding W cannot accidentally shift-click an item out of a moving inventory. onDisable releases every forced pressed flag, but only when the physical key is up or a screen is still open, so the cleanup cannot fight an active key press. The jump and sprint bindings are part of the forced set, which is what makes the module heavier than a walk-only InvMove: the server sees jumps and sprint transitions under an open window, not just horizontal drift.

Vanilla clients freeze in place under a screen because the GUI swallows the movement input. The module's forced flags make the server receive position-changing C03 packets, sprint-state C0B packets and movement for a player whose server-side window is still open, a contradiction the inventory-move checks validate. CheaterDeleter flags position changes under a live screen handler, Photon scores movement past a breaking-time leniency and any jump, Negativity scores distance and sprint and sneak transitions from Bukkit events, and Hawk flags rotation, sprint or sneak while an inventory is open.

files.label: InventoryMove.kt
files.explanation: The module is a single UpdateEvent handler plus one ClickWindowEvent guard and a cleanup routine. The screen condition combines three checks: the current screen must not be GuiChat, must not be GuiIngameMenu, and when NoDetectable is enabled must not be a GuiContainer. When it passes, the six movement keybindings are re-asserted from GameSettings.isKeyDown, which polls the physical keyboard directly and bypasses the GUI input path entirely. The NoMoveClicks handler then cancels window clicks while movement input is present, and onDisable only clears the forced flags when the key is released or a screen remains open. The tag getter is the AACAdditionPro switch's only effect: it appends the AACAdditionPro label to the module name in the module list.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (movement predicates)
files.explanation: The module's only util dependency. isMoving() (line 302) reads movementInput.moveForward and moveStrafe and gates the NoMoveClicks cancellation, so a click is only cancelled while real walk input is present. The class also carries the isOnGround and isInLiquid predicates used across the LiquidSense Dev movement modules; for this module only the isMoving check matters. The file lives under net/ccbluex/liquidbounce/utils with a .java extension while the module itself is Kotlin, a mix that is normal for this snapshot.

countering.label: InventoryMoveCheck (position change under a screen handler)
countering.explanation: CheaterDeleter's check runs on every serverbound move through PlayerMovementListener.onMovement and keys on the exact module signature: packet.isChangePosition() while player.getCurrentScreenHandler() != null (lines 41-48). After a 500ms grace from the moment the screen opened (lines 58-59), invalidateMove flags when a horizontal delta grows while the server-side velocity on that axis is zero (lines 62-77), which is precisely what forced keybind input produces. The flag is MINOR severity with a 100ms cooldown, and the data resets on window close and on damage (onPlayerDamage extends the grace by 1000ms, lines 99-104). The module's sustained WASD movement past the grace drives deltas that grow against zero server velocity, so the check flags on steady use. Movement that rides server-applied velocity (knockback, a moving platform) or movement confined to the first 500ms after opening does not trip it, and the check skips players near non-solid collision and in spectator.

countering.label: InventoryMove (movement and jump under an open inventory)
countering.explanation: Photon's InventoryMove listens on PlayerMoveEvent and skips everything that is not real movement: squared distance at or below 0.005, vehicles, flight, no open inventory, damage invulnerability, liquids, recent teleports or world changes, and low TPS (lines 77-100). The leniency is breakingTime (300ms base plus the speed-potion adjustment, lines 64-71) plus an optional ping leniency; movement past that window with no jump-end grace and no pushing entities flags at 5 VL (lines 134-144). A jump while the inventory is open routes to handleJump at 25 VL, with one allowed jump per open and slab and bounce materials exempted (lines 147-180), and cancel at 60 VL teleports back to the move origin. The module's sustained movement maps onto the walk path and its forced jump binding onto the jump branch, so both penalties are available; the one soft spot is the 300ms breaking window, which brief inventory movement could hide inside.

countering.label: InventoryMoveProtocol (Bukkit-event distance scoring)
countering.explanation: Negativity's protocol is event-based: onMove requires an open inventory (p.getOpenInventory() != null), no elytra, trident, vehicle, water or nearby pistons, fall distance under 0.5 and server velocity at or below 0.1 (lines 33-34), then scores a sprint or sneak transition as 5 points and movement distance at or above the previous move's distance and at or above walk speed as a positive delta (lines 44-56). It flags once timeSinceOpen reaches 3 ticks and the score exceeds 2 (lines 57-63), and isBlockedInFight pauses the protocol during combat. The module's forced sprint binding re-enables sprinting under the open window, which the transition check counts as 5, and sustained walk keeps distance at or above the previous move, so a flag lands from the third tick. Water, pistons, vehicles, fall damage over 0.5 and knockback all silence it, and combat pauses it.

countering.label: InventoryMove (rotation or sprint or sneak while open)
countering.explanation: Hawk's check is the broadest of the set: it flags any MoveEvent where the player updates rotation, sprints or sneaks while hasInventoryOpen() is nonzero and the move is not a teleport accept (line 45), with a violation threshold of 3, a 0.999 decay and a 5 second timeout, punishing with a rubberband. Vanilla sends look updates as part of every C03, so any movement under an open container carries an isUpdateRot flag and trips the check immediately; the module's forced sprint binding is a second independent trigger. The check's own TODO comments concede a one-tick false-positive window after opening and the lack of a teleport grace, so a single early move can slip through, but sustained inventory movement flags on the second move and rubberbands. The NoDetectable carve-out is the module's only honest escape: on non-container screens no container is open server-side, so hasInventoryOpen() reads zero.
